column1: # Book 6 review (Fable, 2026-10-30). No findings. Secondary 6.973 accepted: amaracinum unguentum is the marjoram ointment (marjoram oil), the plant and the ointment one thing. Register: consimili / pari ratione = on a like principle at 6.881 and 6.902; lapis Magnes kept as the Latin names it at 6.908 (the Greeks call it Magnes; the English "magnet" goes in the note), with "this Magnesian stone" at 6.1046 and "the Magnesian stones" at 6.1064. Refrains: 6.923-935 = 4.217-229; 6.924-926 and 6.928-935 take the Book 4 review text verbatim (6.924 and 6.928 keep the Latin's semicolon and the lowercase that follows it; 6.927 differs in the Latin and keeps its own line; 6.923 is the same Latin as 4.217 but the Book 4 English carries "are sent out" from 4.216, so 6.923 reads "bodies that strike" after 6.922's "be sent out"). 6.988-989 = 6.995-996 verbatim. Band: 6.881, 6.890-891, 6.909, 6.946, 6.986, 6.1000-1001; 6.928 and 6.932 are the Book 4 lines and stay as they are.

column2: and a pine torch, lit on a like principle, shines on the waves
Of this kind in the sea at Aradus is the spring of fresh {{NOTE: Aradus, an island city off the Phoenician coast, known for a freshwater spring rising from the seabed.}}
water, that gushes and pushes away the salt waves round it;
it has touched the flame, and a torch on a like principle?
which the Greeks call the Magnes, from its native name, {{NOTE: Magnes lithos, the Magnesian stone, our "magnet"; Lucretius keeps the Greek name, lapis Magnes (6.1046)}}
because it arose within the native bounds of the Magnetes. {{NOTE: The Magnetes, people of Magnesia (in Thessaly, or Magnesia in Lydia); hence "magnet".}}
First, from all the things we see, whatever they are, {{NOTE: 6.921-935 closely repeat 4.216-229; the English repeats its Book 4 lines where the Latin agrees}}
bodies that strike the eyes and provoke the sight.
And from certain things odors flow perpetually;
as cold from rivers, heat from the sun, surge from the waves
of the sea, eater of walls along the shores,
finally, a moisture of salty flavor often comes into the mouth
when we walk beside the sea, and when we watch
in a stream, and sent away in all directions on every side,
and no delay, no rest is granted in the flowing,
since we perpetually feel, and may always
see all things, smell them, and sense them sounding.
All food is spread into the veins, and increases and feeds
Finally, the pig flees marjoram oil and fears every
for we see sounds penetrate by one way, by another flavor
for the rest, from here the reasoning comes easily, and the whole
cause laid open, that lures the force of iron.
